title: Form Your Business Entity with Secretary of State
description: Review business entity filing options with the Washington Secretary of State. Confirm the current forms, fees, and registration process with the agency before filing.
tips: Discuss business structure and tax treatment with an accountant or attorney before choosing an entity.

title: Register with Department of Revenue (DOR)
description: Use your UBI number to register with the WA Department of Revenue for a business tax account. You will need to collect and remit retail sales tax on all construction services. You will also owe B&O (Business and Occupation) tax on gross receipts. Register at My DOR (online portal).
tips: WA charges B&O tax on gross receipts AND retail sales tax on construction labor and materials — including painting and flooring. This is different from most states. File monthly or quarterly depending on revenue.

title: Get Your Contractor License from Labor & Industries (L&I)
description: Check Washington Labor & Industries for the registration or licensing requirements that apply to your trade and planned work. Confirm current application, bond, insurance, and examination requirements with the agency.
tips: Ask Labor & Industries which requirements apply to your business before submitting an application or starting work.

title: Obtain a Surety Bond
description: Check Washington Labor & Industries for any surety bond requirements that apply to your contractor registration. Confirm current amounts and filing instructions with the agency.
tips: Ask an attorney to explain any bond obligations you do not understand before signing.

title: Get General Liability Insurance
description: Check Washington Labor & Industries for the insurance requirements that apply to your registration and planned work. Confirm current requirements with the agency.
tips: Discuss insurance provisions in your contracts with an attorney before choosing coverage.

title: Open a Workers Compensation Account with L&I
description: Check Washington Labor & Industries for workers compensation requirements that apply to your business, owners, and workers. Confirm account and reporting requirements with the agency.
tips: Ask Labor & Industries about coverage options and any exemptions that may apply to your circumstances.

title: Register with Employment Security Department (ESD)
description: Check Washington Employment Security Department for employer registration and unemployment reporting requirements that apply to your business. Confirm filing schedules with the agency.
tips: Discuss payroll reporting responsibilities with an accountant, including any tasks handled by a payroll provider.

title: Set Up Payroll and Tax Reporting
description: Review payroll and tax reporting obligations with an accountant. Check the relevant state agencies and the IRS for current registration, withholding, and filing instructions.
tips: Ask an accountant which records and reporting processes fit your business before choosing a payroll system.

title: Form Your Business Entity on Sunbiz.org
description: Review the business entity options and fictitious-name filing information on Florida's Division of Corporations website. Confirm the current forms and fees with the agency before filing.
tips: Discuss sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, and corporation options with an accountant or attorney before choosing a structure.

title: Determine Your License Requirements
description: Florida requires licensing for many (but not all) construction trades. Check if your trade requires a license through DBPR. Certified licenses are statewide. Registered licenses are county-specific. Some trades like basic painting, flooring installation, and minor handyman work do NOT require licensing in Florida.
tips: Trades that DO require licensing: General Contractor, Building Contractor, Roofing, Plumbing, Electrical, HVAC, Pool/Spa, Solar, Underground Utility. Trades that generally do NOT: Painting, Flooring, Fencing, Pressure Washing, Minor Handyman.

title: Apply for Your Contractor License (If Required)
description: Check the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation for the application requirements that apply to your license type and planned work. Confirm current forms, fees, supporting documents, and examination requirements with the agency.
tips: Ask the licensing agency about current examination instructions and preparation resources for your application.

title: Get General Liability Insurance
description: Check the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation for insurance requirements that apply to your license type and planned work. Confirm current requirements with the agency.
tips: Discuss insurance provisions in your contracts with an attorney before choosing coverage.

title: Set Up Workers Compensation
description: Florida uses PRIVATE insurance for workers comp — there is no state-run fund. If you have employees, you must carry workers comp insurance. Sole owners in construction can apply for an exemption through the Department of Financial Services (DFS), but this means you have no coverage if injured.
tips: Construction employers with 1+ employees MUST carry workers comp in Florida. Officers of corporations are automatically included unless they opt out. LLC members and sole proprietors can apply for an exemption from DFS.

title: Register with Florida Department of Revenue
description: Register for a sales tax certificate with the FL Department of Revenue. In Florida, contractors do NOT pay sales tax on labor — only on materials. This is a significant advantage compared to states like Washington. You may also need to register for reemployment (unemployment) tax.
tips: Major advantage in FL: No sales tax on labor! You only collect/pay sales tax on materials you sell to customers. No state income tax either. This makes Florida one of the most tax-friendly states for contractors.

title: Set Up Payroll (If You Have Employees)
description: Check the Florida Department of Revenue and the IRS for payroll registration, withholding, and reporting requirements that apply to your business. Confirm filing instructions with the relevant agency.
tips: Discuss payroll responsibilities and recordkeeping with an accountant before choosing a payroll system.
